questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Consider how far you live from the campus and if public transport offers a good connection. Otherwise, it can take longer to get to the univserity. For biking: the bike lanes are, if present, not so safe as in CPH. Therefore, one needs to get used to biking here.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are some obligatory courses, some restricted electives and free electives. You chose the course in the catalogue and register. If the course is really small (20 people) you sometimes get on a waiting list, in case the course is already full (usually not the case for obligatory courses, as they are comparably large courses). In the end, some people deregister so that you might still get in. i felt some professors were quite flexible with registering you manually even after deadlines.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an administrative coordinator and there are some webpages to gain information from.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for all the courses was easily possible. The problem is rather in managing overlaps.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
register for everything your interested in. Go to the course the first week and see if you enjoy the teaching style and can handle the workload. if not, for most of the courses you can still deregister within the first two weeks of the semester. 
Watch out for the exam dates. It can happen that you have a super stretched exam phase, starting in december ending in March. or that you have all your exams in 1,2 weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was ok with me as I have had already a lot of courses during my previous studies. Stillt was intense sometimes, as complicated things were mentioned only shortly and not explained as there is no time for this in 1.5 hours per week. And then it is hard to catch up because there are so many courses in one week.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As the courses only take part around 1.5h a week, time is missing to really get into detail or do anything yourself. Mainly its lectures. That I didn't like so much. I enjoyed it a lot in Copenhagen that you have phases were you work yourself and that you have enough hours and days per week to get into a topic. Additionally, in Copenhagen you could focus on your two courses, which is great. At BOKU you need to superficially deal with 7 topics, which is a bit unfulfilling for me.

questions.answer: The ball is in the Wiener Rathhaus which is really beautiful. sport courses to meet people.

questions.answer: Rax/Schneeberg. Hike in the surroundings of Vienna (Wiener Stadtwanderwege). try the good restaurants.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the social activities, do sports courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Relaxed (slow) organisation at institutions. Missing digitalisation.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Enjoying every place, where you can sit outside. The city is so much concrete, but people sit and chill everywhere to share a drink etc. Even if the seats are directly at a big street.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't expect to spent as much time on your courses as you did as UCPH. You need to do so many more than there, so allow yourself to lower the workload per course. 
Gather together in winter. If you don't organise a gathering yourself, you might end up doing nothing/feeling alone.
Come here during summer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The different course structure and learning culture. It is really lecture dominated here.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting closer with my study friends. eat good food and enjoy all the culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The organisation at BOKU, making a schedule that fits my interets and where courses not overlap completely.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
